claim: Paul Delvaux Museum in Sint-Idesbald is the artist's former home/studio, displays over 1,000 m² of the world's largest Delvaux collection, open 10:30-17:30 (last entry 16:45) with seasonal closures on Mon/Tue/Wed outside summer, and currently hosts the exhibition 'Paul Delvaux - Henri-Victor Wolvens: Van verschillen naar overeenkomsten'.
quote: The museum displays more than 1,000 m² of the world's largest collection of this internationally renowned artist. Open from 10:30 to 17:30, last admission 16:45. Standard admission €12, reduced €7-€9, family ticket €34.

claim: Paul Delvaux Museum has reopened after renovation and is fully operational in Sint-Idesbald (P. Delvauxlaan 42), part of Koksijde at roughly 5 km from De Panne.
quote: Museum Paul Delvaux in Sint-Idesbald... since the museum's reopening, it has been buzzing with activity with a beautiful and varied program.

claim: Abdijmuseum Ten Duinen in Koksijde charges €10 adults (26+), €5 ages 19-25, €4 ages 7-18, free under 7, family €25; every first Saturday of the month is free for individuals; South Abbey Mill adds €2 from April-September.
quote: Adults (26+): €10. Ages 19-25: €5. Ages 7-18: €4. Family ticket (up to 5 children and 2 adults): €25. South Abbey Mill (April-September): €2 per person.

claim: Abdijmuseum Ten Duinen sits on the archaeological ruins of the 12th-century Cistercian Duinenabbey in Koksijde and combines a museum with an outdoor archaeological site, located about 7 km from De Panne.
quote: Abdijmuseum Ten Duinen - Koksijde. The museum and archaeological site reveal the story of the Duinenabbey, one of the largest and richest Cistercian abbeys in the Low Countries.

claim: NAVIGO National Fisheries Museum in Oostduinkerke is open Tue-Fri 10:00-17:00/18:00 and Sat/Sun 14:00-17:00/18:00 (seasonal), closed Mondays, with free admission on the first Saturday of each month.
quote: November 1 - March 31: Tuesday-Friday: 10 AM - 5 PM, Saturday-Sunday: 2 PM - 5 PM. April 1 - October 31: Tuesday-Friday: 10 AM - 6 PM, Saturday-Sunday: 2 PM - 6 PM. Closed Mondays.

claim: NAVIGO showcases North Sea aquariums, a fisherman's house, the wooden boat OD 1. Martha, the sperm whale Valentijn and the UNESCO-listed horseback shrimp fishing heritage of Oostduinkerke, around 12 km from De Panne.
quote: North Sea aquariums, a cozy fisherman's house, a wooden fishing boat called OD 1. Martha, historical displays about regional fishermen, a sperm whale named Valentijn.

claim: Museum Cabour (Moeresteenweg 141, De Panne) on the edge of the Cabour dunes covers WWI and WWII history plus the 2/4 Lancers Regiment, with free admission and opening every weekend from Easter to autumn break plus daily during Flemish/Walloon school holidays, 14:00-18:00.
quote: Every day during the Flemish and Walloon holiday periods and every weekend from Easter to autumn break from 2-6 p.m. Closed Mondays and public holidays. Free entry for all visitors.

claim: De Panne's Zeedijk hosts the statue commemorating King Leopold I's landing on Belgian soil on 17 July 1831, and during WWI the Belgian royal family lived there, making De Panne the 'capital of unoccupied Belgium'; the Cabour dunes are the oldest dunes (5000 years) on the Belgian coast and are crossed by a marked heritage walking trail.
quote: On the Zeedijk in De Panne stands an imposing statue honouring King Leopold I, the first King of Belgium, who first set foot on Belgian soil on 17 July 1831... The old dunes of Adinkerke-Ghyvelde are 5000 years old, the oldest dunes on the Belgian coast.

claim: Kunstencentrum Ten Bogaerde in Koksijde is a restored 12th-century Cistercian farmstead with a permanent George Grard sculpture collection in a polder-side garden plus rotating contemporary exhibitions (Panamarenko, Delvaux); entry is often free, and there is a restaurant in the former abbot's residence.
quote: A beautifully restored 12th-century Cistercian farmstead with a sculpture garden overlooking the polders... bronze statues scattered throughout the garden, while his drawings and plaster models are exhibited inside. Entry is often free.

claim: Westfront Nieuwpoort, located beneath the King Albert I Monument at the Ganzepoot lock complex (~17 km from De Panne), tells the WWI story of the polder inundation with a 180° Yser Panorama projection plus lift access to a 360° view; adults €9.50, children 7-18 €6.00, family €24.00, open Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00 (18:00 in July-August).
quote: Adults: €9.50, Children 7-18: €6.00, Family (2 adults + 3 children): €24.00. September 1 - June 30: Tuesday-Sunday, 10 a.m.-5 p.m. July 1 - August 31: Tuesday-Sunday, 10 a.m.-6 p.m.

claim: Plopsaland Belgium in De Panne (renamed from Plopsaland De Panne in summer 2025) originated as Meli Park in 1935 and now has 55 attractions including 7 rollercoasters; it is a theme park rather than a 'Plopsa Story Museum' (no such standalone museum exists, though there is a small K3 museum inside).
quote: In the summer of 2025, the park was renamed from Plopsaland De Panne to Plopsaland Belgium... The park consists of 55 attractions, including 7 rollercoasters. Originally known as Meli Park from 1935 to 1999.

claim: Sint-Idesbald is nicknamed 'Latem-aan-zee' for its artist-village character and concentrates multiple galleries and ateliers around the Paul Delvaux Museum, making it a walkable mini art trail about 4-5 km east of De Panne.
quote: It is an artist village, the 'Latem-aan-zee', with several museums of which that of the world-famous surrealist painter Paul Delvaux is the most well-known.
